texto: The system must allow customers to access their account using login and password.
The system must create a usage session after successful authentication.
The system must allow customers to end their session through logout.
The system must require an active session to access restricted areas, such as customer profile and bookings.
The system must restrict private functionalities to authenticated customers.
The customer session must have limited validity and expire automatically after the configured period.
Logout must invalidate the current session immediately.
Customer personal data must be protected against improper access by other customers.
The system must maintain authentication as a separate capability, responsible exclusively for login, session creation, active session validation, and logout.
The system must allow flight search by informing origin airport, destination airport, and travel date.
The system must allow one-way or round-trip searches.
The system must present the flight options found for each trip segment.
For each flight found, the system must show departure time, arrival time, and reference fare values.
The system must work with a set of previously registered airports.
Flight searches must prioritize fast response, as they represent a recurring customer journey flow.
The system must maintain flight search as an independent capability, responsible for airports, routes, schedules, and reference fares.
The system must allow an authenticated customer to create a booking for a one-way flight.
The system must allow an authenticated customer to create a booking for outbound and return flights in the same operation.
The system must generate an identifier for each created booking.
The system must record the booking date.
The system must inform the customer of the booking identifier after operation completion.
The system must allow customers to consult existing bookings.
The system must present the list of completed bookings.
The system must allow canceling a selected booking.
After cancellation, the booking must no longer appear as active in the customer listing.
The booking capability depends on customer authentication.
The booking capability depends on flight search to obtain available flights.
The system must allow customers to consult their own profile.
The profile must show customer contact data, including phone, phone type, and address.
The system must allow updating contact and address data.
The system must require the current password to confirm profile changes.
The system must prevent customers from viewing or changing another customer profile.
The system must maintain the customer profile as a separate capability from authentication, responsible only for registration and contact data.
The customer profile capability depends on authentication to validate customer access.
The system must show the customer loyalty program status.
The system must show the number of miles accumulated in the year.
The system must show the total accumulated miles.
Loyalty information must be presented as read-only data, not as editable fields.
The system must maintain loyalty as a separate capability from the customer profile, responsible exclusively for status and accumulated miles.
The loyalty capability depends on authentication to validate customer access.
The system must allow initial loading or reloading of the application database.
The loading process must allow defining the number of sample customers to be generated.
The database load must recreate the main operational data, including flights, customers, sessions, and test bookings.
The system must provide summarized operational information, such as numbers of customers, sessions, flights, segments, bookings, and registered airports.
The environment must offer simple ways to prepare and verify the database for tests, demonstrations, or operational reset.
The system must provide basic operational indicators without requiring direct database access.
The system must maintain environment administration as a separate capability, responsible for preparing, reloading, and supervising operational data.
The environment administration capability depends on authentication, flight search, booking, and customer profile to prepare and reset their data.
The application must support high call and query volume, especially in authentication, flight search, and booking flows.
The solution must be suitable for growth without manual support for main self-service operations.
The application must run in different environments, including local infrastructure, public cloud, and hybrid scenarios.
The solution must keep customer, flight, session, and booking data persisted between requests.
Each session and booking must have a unique identifier.
Booking and cancellation operations must maintain enough consistency to correctly reflect the current booking state.
The application must record minimal operational tracking data, such as booking date and operational record counts.
Navigation must support self-service, allowing customers to search flights, manage bookings, and update their profile without human intermediation.
The system must show schedules, dates, and values clearly.
Main journeys must be accessible through a simple web interface, with clear separation among flight search, bookings, profile, and support.
No public customer registration flow was identified. Customer accounts are generated by administrative data loading.
No payment flow, seat selection, or formal fare class selection was identified at booking time; the system shows prices, but the observed booking is simplified.
A Support interface with real-time chat appearance exists, but the corresponding backend was not found. Therefore, this item was not treated as a consolidated functional requirement.
